question: When are injunction and restatement legitimately used?
premises: The distinction of injunction and restatement is real in use but arises only from cognition
It is employed for those who do not yet know synonymous terms
Examples include tree and earth-grower, jar and pot, and the statement that the Great Lord is all this world
inference: Injunction and restatement serve to reveal identity to those who have not yet recognized synonymous expressions of the same reality.
plain_english: The distinction between injunction and restatement is real in practice but arises only from cognition; it is used for those who do not yet know synonymous terms, as in 'this is a tree, an earth-grower' or 'a jar, a pot', and likewise in saying 'the Great Lord is all this world.'
